---
title: "Calculator"
description: "Roughly what not being married costs a couple in Ireland in income tax, inheritance tax and capital gains tax, under 2027 rules."
resources:
  - tax-rules.js
---

Part of [Married, or not](index.qmd). How each tax works, with sources, is on [The cost of not marrying](cost.qmd).

Put in your incomes for two stretches of life, for example while children are small and afterwards, and what one partner might leave the other. The calculator compares what you would pay if you were married with what you pay if you are not. It is a rough estimate, not tax advice.

```{=html}
<form id="mc-form" class="mc-form" onsubmit="return false">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>First stretch</legend>
    <label>Partner 1's income (€ a year) <input type="number" id="a1" min="0" step="1000" value="60000"></label>
    <label>Partner 2's income (€ a year) <input type="number" id="b1" min="0" step="1000" value="0"></label>
    <label>Number of years <input type="number" id="y1" min="0" max="80" step="1" value="5"></label>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Second stretch</legend>
    <label>Partner 1's income (€ a year) <input type="number" id="a2" min="0" step="1000" value="60000"></label>
    <label>Partner 2's income (€ a year) <input type="number" id="b2" min="0" step="1000" value="30000"></label>
    <label>Number of years <input type="number" id="y2" min="0" max="80" step="1" value="25"></label>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Assets</legend>
    <label>What one partner would leave the other (€), for example a half share of the home, savings and pension funds <input type="number" id="inh" min="0" step="5000" value="300000"></label>
    <label>Gains on assets one partner gives the other while both are alive (€), for example moving a property into joint names <input type="number" id="gain" min="0" step="1000" value="0"></label>
  </fieldset>
</form>

<div class="mc-result" aria-live="polite">
  <p class="mc-total-label">Not being married would cost you about</p>
  <p class="mc-total" id="mc-total">€0</p>
  <table class="table mc-table">
    <thead><tr><th></th><th class="text-end">If married</th><th class="text-end">If not married</th><th class="text-end">Difference</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="mc-rows"></tbody>
  </table>
</div>

<script src="tax-rules.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  var T = window.MarriageTax;
  var eur = function (x) { return "€" + Math.round(x).toLocaleString("en-IE"); };
  var ids = ["a1", "b1", "y1", "a2", "b2", "y2", "inh", "gain"];
  function val(id) { var v = parseFloat(document.getElementById(id).value); return isFinite(v) && v > 0 ? v : 0; }
  function row(label, married, single) {
    return "<tr><th scope='row'>" + label + "</th><td class='text-end'>" + eur(married) +
      "</td><td class='text-end'>" + eur(single) + "</td><td class='text-end'><strong>" +
      eur(single - married) + "</strong></td></tr>";
  }
  function update() {
    var y1 = Math.round(val("y1")), y2 = Math.round(val("y2"));
    var incM = y1 * T.incomeTaxMarried(val("a1"), val("b1")) + y2 * T.incomeTaxMarried(val("a2"), val("b2"));
    var incS = y1 * T.incomeTaxSeparate(val("a1"), val("b1")) + y2 * T.incomeTaxSeparate(val("a2"), val("b2"));
    var cat = T.inheritanceTaxCohabitant(val("inh"));
    var cgt = T.cgtCohabitant(val("gain"));
    document.getElementById("mc-rows").innerHTML =
      row("Income tax over " + (y1 + y2) + " years", incM, incS) +
      row("Inheritance tax", 0, cat) +
      row("Capital gains tax", 0, cgt) +
      row("Total", incM, incS + cat + cgt);
    document.getElementById("mc-total").textContent = eur(incS - incM + cat + cgt);
  }
  ids.forEach(function (id) { document.getElementById(id).addEventListener("input", update); });
  update();
})();
</script>
```

## What it assumes

- **Income tax** uses the 2027 rates, bands and credits from Budget 2027, kept the same for every year, with no inflation or pay rises. Incomes are treated as employment income. A married couple pays the lower of joint assessment and being taxed separately. USC and PRSI are left out because they are charged on each person separately either way.
- **Left out, so the real gap can be bigger:** the Home Carer Tax Credit (up to €2,050 a year), which only married couples and civil partners can claim.
- **Inheritance tax** assumes the partner who inherits has had no earlier gifts or inheritances that count towards the same €22,000 threshold, and that no relief applies. The [dwelling house exemption](cost.qmd#inheritance) can cover the family home, if strict conditions are met, and a court order under the Cohabitants Act 2010 is tax free.
- **Capital gains tax** is the tax on a gift between partners that a spouse wouldn't pay. It uses the 31% rate and the €1,270 annual exemption.

The rules are in [`tax-rules.js`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/marriage/tax-rules.js), with a source for each number, and are updated after each Budget.
